title: Symmetric infinity operads, approximations and relative inert sections
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets, full subcategories and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], fibers and cocartesian/cartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], categorical fibrations as the isofibrations of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], and relative mapping spaces and their composition triangle graphs of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. The left-module operadic convention of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] is the special base example; the following definitions allow any symmetric operadic base.

Use the finite pointed-set base, infinity-operad predicate, inert and active edges, and whole-simplex relative diagram category of [def-coef-relative-symmetric-operadic-algebras]. Thus $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ has objects $\langle n\rangle=\{*\}\sqcup\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and all basepoint-preserving functions. A map is inert when each non-basepoint output has exactly one preimage, active when only the basepoint maps to the basepoint. Write $\rho_i:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ for the map retaining only input $i$. Use its nerve $F=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$, canonically lifted to the simplicial-set universe. An infinity operad is an inner fibration $p:P\to F$ of quasicategories with cocartesian lifts of inert maps, the equivalences $P_{\langle n\rangle}\to P_{\langle1\rangle}^n$ induced by those lifts, and the product decomposition of mapping spaces over every pointed map induced by composition with output projections. Inert edges in $P$ are the $p$-cocartesian edges over inert maps. The empty products in both Segal conditions are terminal.

For $r:E\to P$, an operadic fibration is a categorical fibration with cocartesian lifts of inert edges of $P$, transport equivalences $E_x\to\prod_i E_{x_i}$ along each family of inert colour projections $x\to x_i$, and the equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_E^a(y,z)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_E^{a_i}(y,z_i)$ for every base edge $a:r(y)\to r(z)$ and every family of cocartesian output projections $z\to z_i$. The superscript fixes the entire base arrow. Transport is represented by a cylinder over that arrow with cocartesian component edges; composition is represented by the triangle graph with its long-edge normalization. These conditions assert properties, not chosen transports. No active lifts, limits, colimits or presentability are required.

For a categorical fibration $g:D\to P$, being an approximation means: every $d$ over $\langle n\rangle$ has, over each $\rho_i$, a locally $pg$-cocartesian edge whose $g$-image is inert; and every active edge of $P$ ending at $g(d)$ has a $g$-cartesian lift ending at $d$. Locally cocartesian means cocartesian after pullback to the specified base edge. A general $f:C\to P$ is an approximation when it factors over $P$ as an equivalence $C\to D$ followed by such a categorical fibration, with $D$ a quasicategory. Its colour map is the induced map $C\times_F\{\langle1\rangle\}\to P\times_F\{\langle1\rangle\}$ on the original strict fibers.

For a base diagram $b:K\to P$, mark exactly the edges whose $b$-images are inert. Define $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_P(K,E)$ as the full subcategory on inert-preserving vertices in the strict fiber of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,P)$ at $b$. Thus every parameter simplex has constant base diagram, and no invertibility condition is put on transformations. Its sections case is $K=P,b=\mathrm{id}$. Restriction is actual precomposition on the domain coordinate in every simplicial degree. More generally commuting triangles of base diagrams give restriction of lifts, and a target map over $P$ preserving the marked cocartesian edges gives actual postcomposition. These are explicit simplicial maps, without an equivalence assertion.
